stories.h: How To Rob A Bank: Hoult's punky heist is fun but forgettable
sum: David Leitch's new heist comedy stars Nicholas Hoult as Ryan, a former soldier grieving his young son's death from cancer and furious about medical bills. He leads a gang in furry animal costumes that livestreams its bank robberies on YouTube and gives most of the money to charity, while an FBI agent (John C Reilly) and a software developer (Zoe Kravitz) hunt them down.

Screen's Nikki Baughan finds the action kinetic and the vibe infectious, but says the anti-capitalist message drowns in bombast and the script plays both sides. She expects it to pull younger audiences before The Hunger Games prequel arrives a week later.
pts: Rolling out from 11 Nov; US and UK on 13 Nov
Cast includes Zoe Kravitz, Anna Sawai, Pete Davidson
Verdict: kinetic fun, light on conviction

stories.h: Fjord: LWLies savages Mungiu's Sebastian Stan drama
sum: Cristian Mungiu's Fjord follows a Romanian-Norwegian Christian couple (Sebastian Stan and Renate Reinsve) raising five children on the Norwegian coast. They come under a child services investigation after a teacher spots bruises on their eldest daughter.

Little White Lies' David Jenkins calls it a dour, misfired moral drama. He argues it is so one-sidedly hostile to Norway's child services that it plays like propaganda, never makes clear what the parents did, and leaves its children passive. He also finds the lead performances too muted for the story's stakes.
pts: Released 13 Nov; 146 minutes
From the director of 4 Months, 3 Weeks and 2 Days
LWLies scores: enjoyment 1, in retrospect 1

stories.h: Being Heumann: a likeable but tame disability-rights biopic
sum: Siân Heder (CODA) dramatises Judy Heumann's 1977 fight to make Congress enforce Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act, a San Francisco demonstration that became a sit-in. Ruth Madeley plays Heumann, with Dylan O'Brien as a TV reporter who joins the protest and Mark Ruffalo as the official dodging her calls.

LWLies calls it a feelgood, nineties-style throwback with a predictable arc. Madeley is fiery and compelling and the broad ensemble of disabled actors is a plus, but the film is meandering and its political fire often feels tame: more enjoyable than substantial.
pts: Released 13 Nov; also on Apple TV+
Ruth Madeley's lead performance is the highlight
LWLies scores 3 across the board

stories.h: Prima Facie: Cynthia Erivo can't save a flat stage adaptation
sum: Susanna White adapts Suzie Miller's acclaimed one-woman play. Cynthia Erivo plays Tessa, a rising London defence barrister who wins acquittals for men accused of sexual assault, until a colleague (Daniel Ings) rapes her and she faces the system from the other side.

LWLies' Laura Venning says the film loses the play's intensity. Erivo is strong and the use of Tessa's wigs to signal identity is smart, but in the final third she becomes a mouthpiece for the message. The direction is unimaginative and an overused Max Richter piece dilutes the emotion.
pts: Distributed by Sony; out in UK cinemas this week
Timely subject, didactic execution
LWLies scores 2 across the board

stories.h: Brave New Love: a fresh, dreamlike Danish affair drama
sum: Maria Bäck's second feature follows Kate, a Danish hypnotherapist whose three-year affair with a palaeontologist ends when he moves to the Greek island of Samos. The first half mixes domestic realism with broad comedy; the second, set on Samos, blurs reality, myth and dream.

Screen's Boyd van Hoeij, reviewing it at Thessaloniki after its Locarno competition premiere, calls it an impressive, fresh take on infidelity drama. He praises Kathrine Thorborg Johansen's lead and the sharp editing, and its look at loneliness when a woman can't share her heartbreak. Some comic tonal shifts jar, but seem deliberate.
pts: Denmark-Sweden-Greece; score by Jenny Hval
Cast includes Anders Danielsen Lie
Likely niche arthouse release

stories.h: UK-Ireland box office 2026 beats every post-pandemic year
sum: With eight weeks still to go, 2026 UK-Ireland box office has reached £1.07bn, already matching or topping the full-year totals of 2021 to 2025. The year is running 22% ahead of 2025 at the same point, and October alone took £100.6m, up 35% on last year.

Spider-Man: Brand New Day leads the year with £100.3m, ahead of Nolan's The Odyssey (£88.3m) and Toy Story 5 (£58.5m). Verity topped October. The next target is 2019's pre-pandemic £1.35bn, with The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping and You Can See Everything still to come.
pts: 2026 year to date: £1.07bn
October up 35% year on year
Universal has four of the year's top 10

stories.h: First trailer for IDFA documentary Hazara Town
sum: Screen has debuted the first trailer for Hazara Town, the debut feature by Afghanistan-born filmmaker Khadim Dai. It premieres in IDFA's international competition in Amsterdam.

Shot in Quetta, Pakistan, the documentary follows a Hazara family who fled the Taliban two decades ago and now face persecution again. As the threat grows they must choose whether to stay together or leave one by one, knowing they may never reunite. Belgium's Congoo leads production with Australian and German partners, backed by the IDFA Bertha Fund and the Sundance documentary programme.
pts: World premiere in IDFA international competition
Prague-based Filmotor handles world sales
Shot in Quetta, where Hazara still face targeted killings

stories.h: Curzon buys Jodie Comer's taxidermy horror musical Stuffed
stories.why: Offbeat genre pick to watch for
sum: Curzon has acquired UK-Ireland rights to Stuffed, a body-horror musical directed by Theo Rhys that opened TIFF's Discovery section. Jodie Comer plays a reclusive taxidermist who advertises for the perfect human specimen; Harry Melling is the lonely factory worker who answers, afraid of leaving no legacy.

The feature grew out of Rhys's Bafta-nominated short of the same name, with original music by co-writer Joss Holden-Rea. It was developed by the BFI with Ffilm Cymru Wales backing, and Cornerstone handles world sales. Curzon praised its mix of the macabre and the romantic.
pts: Director Theo Rhys is a 2026 Screen Star of Tomorrow
Premiered at Toronto
No UK release date announced yet

stories.h: Letterboxd's November Watchlist This picks
sum: Letterboxd Journal's monthly roundup of bubbling-under films picks five titles. Victorian Psycho is a gory period satire with Maika Monroe as a governess unleashing her darkest impulses. Paul Thomas Anderson's Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall is a concert film shot with Benny Safdie on camera.

Marie Kreutzer's Gentle Monster, about a pianist whose husband is investigated for abuse imagery, streams on Netflix from 18 November. Andrey Zvyagintsev's Cannes Grand Prix winner Minotaur heads to MUBI, and Siân Heder's Being Heumann is on Apple TV+.
pts: Gentle Monster on Netflix from 18 Nov
Minotaur streaming on MUBI
Most picks open in select US cinemas first

stories.h: Coachella 2027: Tame Impala, Dua Lipa and SZA headline
sum: Coachella has revealed its 2027 bill. The festival returns to the Empire Polo Club in Indio over two weekends, April 9–11 and April 16–18, with long-rumoured headliners Dua Lipa, Tame Impala and SZA at the top. Daddy Yankee gets a quasi-headliner slot at the foot of the poster, and Madonna is booked in the dance tent.

For indie and alt-rock fans the undercard is strong: Phoebe Bridgers, Weezer, a returning Pinegrove (on hiatus since 2023), American Football, Caroline Polachek, Gang Of Youths, Magdalena Bay, Social Distortion, The Damned, MUNA and Lambrini Girls. Robyn, Four Tet, Underworld and the Avalanches round out the electronic side.
pts: Two weekends: April 9–11 and 16–18, 2027
Phoebe Bridgers, Weezer, Pinegrove and American Football on the bill
No Beyoncé or Kendrick Lamar this time

stories.h: Gang Of Youths announce Compañero, share "Benny's Video"
sum: Australian rockers Gang Of Youths will release Compañero, their first album in five years, on March 12, 2027. The 11-track record follows August's single "Things Take Time" and, per Stereogum, dwells on mortality even though it came out of a calm period in the band's lives.

The new single "Benny's Video", named after Michael Haneke's 1992 film, is a fast, synth-driven track that builds to a surging climax built for live shows. The band also announced a spring North American tour running from Boston on March 17 through Brooklyn, Chicago, Seattle and San Francisco, slotting in both Coachella weekends.
pts: Compañero out March 12, 2027 (11 tracks)
First album in five years
North American tour March–April plus Coachella

stories.h: Faith No More reunite with Trey Spruance for 2027 tour
sum: Faith No More's 2027 reunion, their first tour in 11 years, will feature guitarist Trey Spruance, Mike Patton's Mr. Bungle co-founder. Spruance played on 1995's King For A Day... Fool For A Lifetime but never toured with the band; Jon Hudson, who held the role after the 2009 reunion, appears to be out.

The lineup is Spruance, Patton, Roddy Bottum, Billy Gould and Mike Bordin. The 16 announced dates run from a January 15 stadium show at Rio's Maracanã through Australia and New Zealand to European rock festivals, ending at Lisbon's NOS Alive on July 9. The only US stops are Welcome To Rockville and Sonic Temple.
pts: First Faith No More tour in 11 years
Trey Spruance replaces Jon Hudson on guitar
16 dates, Rio to Lisbon, January–July 2027

stories.h: King Gizzard announce second techno album of 2026, Entropy
sum: King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard will release Entropy on December 4 via their own (p)doom label. It is a companion to Alien Metal, which came out under three months ago, and both grew from long jams on the band's Eurorack modular synth rig. Entropy runs faster, at 160 bpm, and sounds more cosmic and harmonic than its grittier sibling.

The first single, "Rogue Wave", is heavy on vocal effects and recalls their 2021 synth record Butterfly 3000. The band also set 2027 North American tours for August and October, including the Gorge and two nights at Hollywood Forever, and confirmed their Field of Vision festival won't return to Colorado.
pts: Entropy out December 4, eight tracks
Lead single "Rogue Wave"
2027 North American tour; tickets on sale November 13
stories.q: King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard Rogue Wave

stories.h: Conor Oberst plans 49-date solo tour, from a cave to The Shining hotel
sum: Bright Eyes leader Conor Oberst will play his first solo headline tour since 2019, An Alleged Evening With Conor Oberst. The 49 dates run from February 19, 2027 in Lawrence, Kansas, to a two-night close at Colorado's Stanley Hotel, the place that inspired The Shining.

Unusual rooms are the theme: the underground Caverns in Tennessee, Big Sur's Henry Miller Memorial Library, San Francisco's Castro Theatre and a former monastery chapel in Tucson. One dollar per ticket goes to his Poison Oak Project for trans and LGBTQ+ equity. Bright Eyes also have three Brooklyn Paramount album shows in January.
pts: 49 dates, February–May 2027
Stanley Hotel finale on May 14–15
Tickets on sale November 13

stories.h: Eterna's Push trades slacker fuzz for post-rock bliss
sum: Eterna is Guillem Peeters, the Barcelona-born, London-based former drummer of bar italia. On his third album, Push, The Line of Best Fit hears him leave behind the scruffy lo-fi slacker sound of his first two records for something patient, hazy and post-rock leaning, with Talk Talk-style slow builds and tactile, fragmented guitar solos.

The review praises "Kyrie", where everything locks into place, the magnificent "Shadowcasting for the Villain", the trip-hop mood of "Gum" and the pastoral closer "Rex". Its verdict: a big step up from a cult slacker act to a confident, immersive artist.
pts: Third album from ex-bar italia drummer
Talk Talk and early post-rock comparisons
Highlights: Kyrie, Shadowcasting for the Villain

stories.h: Tove Styrke turns inward on an afterparty concept album
sum: Tove Styrke's second album of 2026, I thought this story wasn't about me, is a concept record set over a dusk-to-dawn afterparty, built around the image of someone alone in a crowd. The Line of Best Fit finds it more introspective and experimental than her dance-pop past, drawing on cinematic textures and early-2000s indie and electronic beats, with LCD Soundsystem and David Lynch as touchstones.

Highlights include the club-ready opener "Prayer", the wordless, filmic "Let's Go Camping", the short Eno-like "Afterparty Hymn" and the haunting "Space". Shaped by a break from music and becoming a parent, it is judged a personal, risk-taking triumph.
pts: Dusk-to-dawn afterparty concept
Indie and electronic textures over pure pop
Highlights: Prayer, Afterparty Hymn, Space
stories.q: Tove Styrke I thought this story wasn't about me

stories.h: Thee Marloes get a Hiroshi Fujiwara remix and 7-inch
sum: Surabaya trio Thee Marloes have teamed up with Japanese producer and fashion figure Hiroshi Fujiwara on a remix of "What's On Your Mind", from their album Di Hotel Malibu. The remix came out on November 9, and Fujiwara also designed its 7-inch vinyl. Staple founder Jeff Staple joins as a producer and adds an exclusive variant for his New York store.

The vinyl is on pre-order via the BCR Webstore and Bandcamp and reaches record shops in several countries from November 20. Pophariini frames the collaboration as a push into international markets, ahead of a December Asia tour taking in Pattaya, Taipei, Seoul and Singapore.
pts: Remix out November 9; 7-inch in shops November 20
Jeff Staple variant sold in New York
Asia tour in December
stories.q: Thee Marloes What's On Your Mind Hiroshi Fujiwara remix

stories.h: Barasuara's Iga Massardi goes solo with pop single "Ambivalensi"
sum: Iga Massardi, known for rock bands Barasuara, Portura and The Mets, released his first solo single, "Ambivalensi", on November 9. It is a mellow, romantic pop song about the hesitation that makes people keep falling-in-love feelings to themselves, and it ends deliberately unresolved.

Iga says he grew up on Indonesian pop like Bebi Romeo and Naif, and friend Vega Antares produced it with an oldies feel. He first meant to give the song to other singers, but friends talked him into singing it himself. More songs will follow next year and be collected into a solo EP.
pts: Solo debut from the Barasuara frontman
Produced by Vega Antares
Solo EP to be built from 2027 singles

stories.h: Couldn't check Beyoncé or Kendrick Lamar news today
sum: Rolling Stone and Billboard blocked fetching this morning, so the watchlist check couldn't be done. Nothing was confirmed either way.

stories.h: adidas x Drama Call ClimaCool 1 GTX goes lime and starry
stories.why: Playful niche label, pop of lime
sum: Manchester label Drama Call and adidas Originals are back for their fourth collab, a ClimaCool 1 GTX built for the city's endless rain. Founder Charlie Bows wrapped it in black ripstop with a GORE-TEX membrane, then added a marbled lime, black and grey camo outsole with a maroon edge line.

The fun is in the details: pulse-lime piping, lime sockliners covered in halftone stars, three silver stars on the heel and a metal star hangtag on a ball chain. It drops November 14 on dramacall.com, then November 15 on the adidas CONFIRMED app and at select retailers. Price isn't confirmed yet.
pts: Drops Nov 14 (Drama Call), Nov 15 (adidas CONFIRMED)
Waterproof GORE-TEX with a lime camo sole
Star graphics, silver hardware, cord-lock laces

stories.h: CPFM's Nike Flea 1 lands in deep 'Cave Purple'
stories.why: Bold color on a weird, chunky shoe
sum: Cactus Plant Flea Market's Nike Flea 1 is getting a moody purple colorway, and LeBron James was the first to be spotted in it. The chunky shoe mixes Dunk and Air Force 1 DNA, with a rich purple suede upper, geometric textured overlays, an oversized padded tongue and a thick collar.

The midsole is a dark purple with a dirt-like texture, and a black-and-white embroidered yin-yang sits on the heel. It's expected to cost $180 and is rumored for Holiday 2026, likely through a CPFM raffle alongside a 'Barley' pair. Nike hasn't confirmed the release yet.
pts: Rumored Holiday 2026 raffle, not confirmed
Purple suede with a yin-yang heel

stories.h: Seoul's Ojos and Sorel launch starry winter footwear
stories.why: Niche Asian label, quirky star details
sum: Seoul womenswear label Ojos has teamed up with Sorel for its first global collab, called 'Stars on the Ground'. It pairs Sorel's cold-weather know-how with Ojos's habit of turning technical materials into something experimental and wearable day to day.

There are two styles. The Ona Avenue Alpine Tall is a waterproof suede boot in Ojos's signature gray, with a shearling tongue, fleece lining, insulation and swappable laces. The Ambler Fireside is a waterproof clog inspired by Sorel's Caribou boot, finished in faded gray with star details. It's on sale from November 12 at ojos.kr and Ojos stores, where in-store buyers get free leg warmers while they last.
pts: On sale Nov 12 at ojos.kr and Ojos stores
Tall boot plus a star-detailed clog
Free leg warmers in store while stocks last

stories.h: Stella McCartney x Yoshitomo Nara go 'rock'n'roll forest'
sum: Stella McCartney and Japanese artist Yoshitomo Nara are back with their third limited collaboration. The theme is a 'rock'n'roll forest', with Nara's mischievous kid characters and animals spread across knitwear in responsibly sourced wool, organic cotton jersey separates, vegan bags and graphic trainers printed with his art.

Four extra-limited atelier pieces include framed hand-crocheted faces plus knitted scarves and jumpers, some taking more than 60 hours to make. Actor Ryo Ryusei and model Mika Schnider front the campaign, and Japan gets pop-ups and collectible stickers. The collection launched globally on November 11 on Stella McCartney's site. Prices weren't listed.
pts: Out now on stellamccartney.com (since Nov 11)
Nara-print trainers and cartoon knitwear
Hand-crocheted atelier pieces in tiny numbers

stories.h: Telfar's FW26 drop: leopard, snake and $68 skullies
sum: Telfar's site is leading with its New FW26 Collection, a big mix of tailoring, workwear, cargo and several denim washes, from raw blue to 'dirty' black. The fun corner is the leopard and snake pieces: baby tees, snoods, thumbhole tops and leggings, mostly $105 to $290.

For cheaper ways in, there are skullies at $68 each in leopard red, snake tan, star green and signature blue, and a new Baby Bag Charm at $78. The charm comes in 12 colors, including Glow in the Dark, Acid, Azalea and Yellow, and only Black Rainbow is sold out. Spend $200 and you get a free logo hat.
pts: Baby Bag Charm $78, 12 colors incl. glow-in-the-dark
Skullies $68 in leopard, snake and star
Free hat on orders of $200+

stories.h: Silly, sexy fits at London's new queer rave Pouffe
sum: Dazed went to the second edition of Pouffe, a queer rave at Tottenham's Unit 58 run by William Craven, Jam and Billy. The name takes back a slur the hosts heard growing up, and the whole point is joy over cool-kid posturing. Billy built a giant fuzzy rainbow mascot, the DJ booth was covered in hands and tentacles, and Czech Hunter Schafer interviewed guests at the door.

There's no dress code, so people dressed to dance and sweat: sporty shorts, cropped vests, lace mesh and studded bras, plus vintage furs thrown over printed silk slips and a Carmela Soprano tee. Craven sums up the vibe as sexy and a bit silly.
pts: Sportswear mixed with lingerie and vintage fur
Rainbow fuzzy mascot sets the playful tone
No dress code, just dressed to dance

stories.h: This week's drops: Elliott Smith Supreme, Metallica x MADSAKI
stories.why: Rock merch and playful drops in one list
sum: Hypebeast's weekly list has a strong rock thread. Supreme's seven-piece Elliott Smith capsule uses album-era photos and lands November 12 (Asia on the 14th). Metallica and artist MADSAKI return with coach and varsity jackets, caps and badges on November 14 via PARADISE TOKYO, in limited numbers.

Also on the list: Palace Winter Drop 7 with a puffer in six colors (November 13), LOEWE x The Nightmare Before Christmas (November 12), Billionaire Boys Club x Pokémon for the 30th anniversary (November 13), Kith x Knicks, Oakley x Metalwood and a black cashmere-linen set from Kaptain Sunshine x COVERCHORD. No prices were listed.
pts: Supreme x Elliott Smith out Nov 12
Metallica x MADSAKI out Nov 14, limited
BBC x Pokémon and Palace puffers Nov 13

stories.h: Inside the Tokyo home of Hysteric Glamour's founder
sum: i-D visited Nobuhiko Kitamura, who started Hysteric Glamour in Tokyo in 1984 by mixing '70s punk, Warhol-style pop art and vintage Americana. He says the name came from the energy of female rock singers like Blondie and Patti Smith. His home is full of stories: a gift from Sofia Coppola, the Herman Makkink sculptures seen in A Clockwork Orange, and links to Patti Smith, whose Polaroid book he later published.

Kitamura says his Davide Sorrenti campaigns were candid snaps of friends, not staged shoots. He's critical of corporate trend cycles and AI-driven references, and thinks Japanese street style today is more about baggy fits and logos than subcultures.
pts: Hysteric Glamour was born from punk and rock
Published Patti Smith's Polaroid book
Says today's street style lacks subculture

stories.h: DPR factions back move toward Gibran impeachment
stories.why: Dynasty politics cracking; civil liberties at stake
sum: Konde.co reports that on 11 November eight DPR factions agreed to use the House's right to express an opinion (HMP) over Vice President Gibran's disputed school-equivalency document, with 120 of 580 members proposing his removal. The trigger was a 30 October Supreme Court ruling that voided the 2019 equivalency certificate, finding no proof he finished secondary school abroad.

The piece stresses this is not yet impeachment: a plenary needs a two-thirds quorum and vote, then a special committee and a Constitutional Court ruling. Gibran reportedly weighed resigning after meeting Prabowo but wants to fight in court. The author warns elite infighting could bring curbs on free expression and assembly.
pts: Eight factions, 120 MPs back HMP route
Supreme Court voided Gibran's equivalency document
Formal impeachment still needs two-thirds plenary vote

stories.h: Rempang residents reported to police over school site
stories.why: Land conflict and criminalisation of residents
sum: Mongabay Indonesia reports that five Rempang residents in Batam were reported to police after entering the construction site of a 'Sekolah Terintegrasi Merah Putih' on land BP Batam claims under an 18.5-hectare management right (HPL). The reports cite criminal code articles on trespass and obstructing officials.

YLBHI, Walhi and a national solidarity team call it criminalisation meant to intimidate residents defending ancestral land, and have filed complaints with Komnas HAM, Kompolnas, the Ombudsman and the witness protection agency. Residents say they don't oppose the school but want land status settled first. The land agency says the HPL process was clean; the Ombudsman earlier found maladministration.
pts: Five villagers face trespass and obstruction reports
Rights groups call it criminalisation
Ombudsman found maladministration in land process

stories.h: Grassroots women challenge Job Creation Law in court
stories.why: Women, land rights and the Omnibus Law
sum: Mongabay Indonesia reports on a Constitutional Court challenge (case 307/PUU-XXIV/2026) filed in August by Solidaritas Perempuan with four women from communities hit by development: Indigenous women of Poco Leok facing a geothermal project, Makassar fisherwomen squeezed by a new port, Poso farmers affected by a hydropower plant, and Watutau Indigenous women threatened by the land bank policy.

They contest five provisions covering land acquisition, environmental impact assessments, the land bank and strict liability, arguing the law denies women meaningful participation in national strategic projects. Hearings with expert and fact witnesses continue; petitioners criticised repeated government postponements. No ruling has been issued.
pts: Five Omnibus Law articles contested
Petitioners from four project-affected communities
Government sought repeated postponements

stories.h: Settlers who attack return in army uniform, probe finds
stories.why: Documents state backing of settler violence
sum: An Al Jazeera investigation reports that settlers who attack Palestinians in the occupied West Bank often come back in military uniform to give orders, using facial matching and testimony to identify individuals, including one previously on, then removed from, a US sanctions list. It says 14 of 63 Palestinians killed by settlers since October 2023 were shot by people serving in or wearing army uniform.

The report says the army's regional defence battalions, largely settler reservists, have grown sixfold since 2023, and cites Yesh Din data that 93.6% of police cases against settlers since 2005 closed without indictment. Palestinian farmers' union and Israeli critics describe army and settlers as effectively merged.
pts: 14 of 63 settler killings by uniformed men
Settler-staffed defence units grew sixfold
93.6% of settler cases closed without charges

stories.h: UK keeps awarding contracts to settlement-linked firms
sum: Al Jazeera finds that UK public bodies awarded £10.7m ($14.4m) in new contracts to companies tied to West Bank settlements after Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband announced powers on 8 September to sanction firms profiting from them. Using procurement data from Tussell, it counts 18 new contracts since then.

Firms named include Heidelberg Materials, whose Israeli subsidiary is linked to a quarry near Qalqilya, Motorola Solutions, Fosun and Egis, all listed in the UN settlement database. Heidelberg says quarry operations ceased in 2023; Egis disputes its listing. A law professor says the firms appear to breach humanitarian law, and Jeremy Corbyn called the contracts outrageous. The Cabinet Office did not comment.
pts: £10.7m in new deals since sanctions pledge
All firms appear in UN settlement database
Fuel for local BDS procurement campaigns

stories.h: Gaza floods swamp tents as drainage lies in ruins
sum: Heavy rain has flooded large parts of Gaza, Al Jazeera reports. The Government Media Office says 70,000 tents were submerged or damaged, affecting about 350,000 people, and that over 700km of sewage network has been destroyed. Civil Defence says it received more than 2,000 distress calls in 12 hours but could answer only 218, citing fuel shortages and broken equipment.

Gaza City's municipality says it lost about 85% of its vehicle fleet in the war and now runs on one bulldozer and two suction trucks, with drainage at roughly a fifth of capacity. Officials say caravans promised under the October 2025 ceasefire are stuck at the border and aid falls far short of needs.
pts: 70,000 tents flooded, officials say
Only 218 of 2,000+ calls answered
Promised caravans held at border

stories.h: Hebron residents report looting after 11-day siege
stories.why: Collective punishment in occupied West Bank
sum: +972 Magazine reports that Palestinians in Hebron's Al-Jilda and Deir Bahha neighbourhoods returned after an 11-day Israeli military operation (23 October to 2 November) to find homes ransacked and gold, cash and goods missing. At least 619 families, about 3,971 people, were displaced after a shooting that killed two Israeli soldiers.

Car dealers in Farsh Al-Hawa say around 300 vehicles were taken, with losses in the millions of shekels. Residents held daily protests demanding return. The army told +972 the operation targeted militant infrastructure, that forces were ordered to protect property, and that specific claims would be investigated; the magazine notes only four weapons were seized.
pts: About 3,971 people displaced
Residents allege theft of savings and cars
Army says claims will be investigated

stories.h: US widens case against Michigan Palestine activists
sum: Mondoweiss reports that federal prosecutors added four recent University of Michigan graduates to a conspiracy case against pro-Palestine activists, bringing defendants to 12. Charges include conspiracy to transmit threats and to intimidate a witness. The authors say FBI agents raided homes on 29 October and switched off body cameras.

Prosecutors also sought to revoke one defendant's bond, citing messages they called antisemitic; Judge Judith Levy said the record showed no antisemitism, eased another defendant's conditions, and called the US Attorney's press release comparing activists to Hitler very concerning. A bond hearing is set for 18 November. The authors note no terrorism or hate-crime charges were filed.
pts: 'Michigan 8' becomes 'Michigan 12'
Judge rebuked prosecutors' Hitler comparison
Bond hearing set for 18 November
